thread:
maria: Headed a customer escalation — ACME reported a sudden spike of 502/504s on Hosted API when sending large embedding batches around 09:03 UTC. They say it started after they increased parallel uploads to 12x. Sample curl got a 504. Sharing logs and repro below.

ingress-bot: Alert: 504-rate from edge-gateway eu-west-1 cluster; spike at 2026-03-20T09:03:12Z — 45 errors / 1m. Top upstream: embed-v2-pool.

nate: Thx @maria. Can you paste minimal repro curl and any request-id from the customer? Also which model/route?

maria: Route: POST /v1/embeddings model=embed-large-v2 tenant=acme-corp
Customer request-id: 01H8X2Y7A9QZ
Repro curl (they ran locally):
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"inputs": ["...big-payload..."], "batch_size": 8192}' 
```
Response snippet: `HTTP/2 504` and sometimes `HTTP/2 502` with upstream reset.

alex: Seeing a coincident ejection of several embed-v2 instances from LB around the same time. Envoy stats show repeated `upstream_rq_5xx` and `ejected` flags. Could be healthcheck sensitivity + long request processing holding connections.

nate: Can you paste the small envoy metric dump? Also check if eus embed pool had a JVM/native OOM or kernel ulimit?

maria: Pasted a trimmed snippet from edge logs: 
```
[09:03:11Z] incoming req id=01H8X2Y7A9QZ route=/v1/embeddings size=5.2MB conn=keepalive
[09:03:12Z] upstream embed-v2-12 request forwarded pid=embed-12
[09:03:13Z] upstream embed-v2-12 timeout 30s -> envoy return 504 id=01H8X2Y7A9QZ
[09:03:13Z] embed-12 process busy: latency=28s mem=82%
[09:03:14Z] envoy: host embed-12 marked unhealthy (consec5xx=4)
```
No OOM logs on the host; CPU high, network rx saturating.

alex: That makes me think: large batch requests keep KV cache pinned and block worker threads. LB healthcheck config currently ejects hosts after 3 consecutive 5xx within 1m with aggressive outlier detection. During a localized burst, this causes cascade ejection -> fewer hosts -> higher queueing -> more 504s.

nate: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: reduce ejection sensitivity and/or increase min hosts for that pool, and throttle incoming concurrency per-tenant. I can patch the outlier detector for embed-v2 pool to 6 consecutive 5xx for the next 30m to see if it stabilizes.

maria: Customer needs immediate workaround — advised them to drop parallelism from 12 -> 4 and retry. They confirmed errors drop after throttling. Would appreciate rollback-safe change.

alex: I'll prepare a conservative change: increase `consecutive_5xx` threshold to 6 and set `enforcement_interval` to 1m for embed-v2. Will do a staged rollout: canary 1/10 for 5m, watch `upstream_ejects` and `latency_p95`.

support-bot: Recorded action: escalation ticket #ESC-2026-129 created. Assigned to @alex and @nate.

maria: Thanks — please post observed metric delta after canary. I'll update ACME and ask them to keep concurrency low for next 2 hours.

nate: Quick Q: should we also add a token-level concurrency cap in API gateway for embeddings? Could prevent tenant blasts.

alex: Good idea. I can add a per-tenant in-flight limit (default 8) behind a feature flag; we can enable for high-risk tenants after QA. Not for immediate patch but tracked.

maria: Perfect. Closing loop for now — mitigation (customer throttle) confirmed, LB config change planned. Will update once canary completes. :thumbsup:
